# Set up the project right

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-blocks.mjs from scripts/blocks-meta.json. Edit that file, not this one. -->

### Git
- What: Keeps a history of every change, so any mistake can be undone.
- Applies when: every app.
- Stage: day-one
- Kind: checkable
- Scope: setup
- Proof: test
- Done when: The project is a git repository, with its first commit on the work branch, not on the main branch.

### Branches
- What: A separate line of work, so changes can be tried without touching the main version.
- Applies when: every app.
- Stage: day-one
- Kind: checkable
- Scope: setup
- Proof: test
- Done when: Build work happens on a branch, not directly on the main branch.

### venv
- What: Gives a Python project its own set of packages, separate from every other project.
- Applies when: the project uses Python.
- Stage: day-one-if
- Kind: checkable
- Scope: setup
- Proof: test
- Done when: Packages install into an environment that belongs to this project only, and a fresh install from the requirements file works.

### Env vars
- What: Settings that change per machine, such as keys and addresses, live outside the code.
- Applies when: every app.
- Stage: day-one
- Kind: checkable
- Scope: setup
- Proof: test
- Done when: Settings that differ per machine come from the environment, and the app starts from the example env file once its values are filled in.

### Secrets
- What: Keys and passwords are kept out of the code, out of git and out of logs.
- Applies when: every app.
- Stage: day-one
- Kind: checkable
- Scope: setup
- Proof: test
- Done when: The real env file is ignored by git, the app reads every key and password from the environment, and the example env file holds no real values.
